newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa truth body cancels prickly media probe.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa truth body cancels prickly media probe.

text.p: South Africa's truth commission said on Friday it had cancelled a deal for a white-led media institute to prepare a report on press coverage in the apartheid years, after protests from black journalists and editors.

Black journalist and editor groups told the commission this week they thought people from the Freedom of Expression Institute (FXI) who were to carry out the probe were tainted themselves by having worked in the white apartheid-era press.

"In the light of representations to the commission, the human rights violations committee has decided to rescind the mandate it gave to the FXI," a statement by the Truth and Reconciliation Commission (TRC) said.
Black Editors' Forum chairman Thami Mazwai has argued that the FXI should not handle the probe because some of its white members were part of a system that discriminated against black journalists.
"Even when the state was implementing its various restrictive laws, there was very little opposition from the English media," Mazwai said.
The TRC suffered another setback this week when senior black members complained to the press that they were being sidelined by a "clique of white liberals" in crucial policy discussions.
TRC chairman, Archbishop Desmond Tutu, dismissed their complaints. His body is tasked with uncovering human rights violations that took place during four decades of apartheid rule.
